title: Death Valley
subject: Science
source: NYSED 2024 Grade 8 ILS Released Items, Questions 33-38
directions: Base your answers to questions 33 through 38 on the information below and on your knowledge of science.

intro.html: Death Valley National Park, located on the border of California (CA) and Nevada (NV), is the largest national park in the continental U.S. It has the lowest elevation in North America at 282 feet below sea level and contains the driest desert in North America. Rock strata in the Death Valley region can provide evidence for the geologic history of the area. The oldest rocks are metamorphic and are approximately 1.7 billion years old. Sedimentary rocks in the valley region are about 500 million years old and are evidence that the area was the site of a warm shallow sea. Igneous rock layers are believed to range from 65.5 to about 2 million years old when volcanic ash and cinder from nearby volcanoes covered the region.

flats.html: In February 2005, Badwater Basin in Death Valley received about six inches of rain from streams flowing into the enclosed basin that flooded the area. The photographs below show this region shortly after the flood in February 2005 and again in February 2007, in which mineral salt deposits are clearly visible.

flats.caption: February 2005
flats.alt: Gray-scale aerial photograph labeled February 2005 with a north arrow and a 2 km scale bar. A darker flooded area is labeled in the middle of Badwater Basin, salt deposits are labeled on the lighter ground at lower left, Death Valley is labeled at the bottom, and the Amargosa Range is labeled on the dark mountains at the right.

flats.caption: February 2007
flats.alt: Gray-scale aerial photograph labeled February 2007 of the same area, with a north arrow and a 2 km scale bar. Death Valley is labeled at the top, Badwater Basin in the center, salt deposits near the bottom of the bright area, and the Amargosa Range on the dark mountains at the right.

flats.html: The salt flats region in Death Valley covers over 200 square miles. Salt flat formation requires:

items: a large basin where streams carry salts down to the basin
an enclosed basin, like Death Valley, where the salts dissolved in stream water can be trapped and not wash away
an arid climate with high temperatures to drive water cycle processes

items.stem: Which list identifies the names of the missing processes, numbered 1 through 3, of the rock cycle?
Which two sources of energy are responsible for the cycling of Earth materials and the flow of energy, as shown in the rock cycle model?
options: the Sun and Earth’s hot interior
Earth’s hot interior and the Moon’s hot interior
evaporation and condensation of water on Earth’s surface
the Sun’s energy and Earth’s magnetic fields

items.stem: Which piece of evidence would support the claim that Death Valley National Park is the result of past tectonic plate motions?
options: Death Valley is the lowest elevation in North America.
The locations of the mountain ranges on either side of Death Valley are almost parallel to each other.
There is thick sediment on the bottom of Death Valley.
There are uplifted mountain ranges on either side of Death Valley.

items.stem: Identify one water cycle process that is directly responsible for the formation of the large mineral salt flats in Death Valley and explain how this process is driven by energy from the Sun. [1]
rubric: Allow 1 credit for evaporation and an acceptable explanation. Acceptable responses include, but are not limited to:

— Water is heated by energy from the Sun, making water molecules on the surface of the water move faster and escape into the air as water vapor.
— Energy from the Sun warms the surface of the water, causing water molecules to move into the air as a gas, leaving salt behind.
items.exemplar:
Process: evaporation
Explanation: Water is heated by energy from the Sun, making water molecules on the surface of the water move faster and escape into the air as water vapor.

items.stem: Using the data as evidence, predict the season (spring, summer, fall, or winter) during which a flood is most likely to occur in Death Valley, California. Also, explain how the data provides evidence for your prediction. [1]
rubric: Allow 1 credit for winter and an acceptable explanation. Acceptable responses include, but are not limited to:

— The data shows the greatest precipitation occurring in December, January, February, and March, which are winter months.
— The winter months of December, January, February, and March, have the greatest amounts of precipitation.
items.exemplar:
Season: winter
Explanation: The data shows the greatest precipitation occurring in December, January, February, and March, which are winter months.

items.stem: Which statement is a reasonable action that could be taken by Death Valley Park officials to mitigate the effects of flash floods or flooding events for park visitors?
options: Based on seasonal rainfall data, place barrels throughout the park to catch some of the extra rainfall.
Use precipitation data to decide when to post road closures and detours in areas that typically flood.
When any rainfall occurs, close the entire national park to prevent loss of property and life.
Build barriers along the sides of all roads in the national park to keep flood waters off the road at times of high precipitation events.
